target.description: Decode the Bayes-optimal prior from pre-stimulus neural activity; retain movement-predictor and pseudosession controls. Better prior decoding does not prove causal prior computation.

dataset.description: Paper identifies the 2024 IBL release and separate WFI recordings; registration pins the 2023_12_bwm_release loader family. Exact versioned input manifest and modality coverage are not yet reconciled.

cohort.description: Journal regional analyses contain 414 Ephys sessions/242 regions/2,289 region-sessions and 51 WFI sessions/32 regions/1,539 region-sessions. The exact roster must be recovered, including the separate 171-session movement subset.

split.description: Ephys uses nested interleaved fivefold outer and fivefold inner trial CV; WFI uses 50 outer folds and leave-one-out inner CV. Ten random splits are repeated. New held-mouse/session testing changes the original task.

inputs.description: Ephys binned spike counts and WFI pixel fluorescence are modality-specific inputs; behavior/video predictors are controls, not extra oracle information for the neural decoder.

preprocessing.description: Ephys sums spikes from -600 to -100 ms and uses Lasso; WFI uses frame -2 and Ridge. Preserve published QC, reaction-time and minimum-trial/unit/pixel inclusion.

metric.description: R-squared measures prior decoding; corrected R-squared subtracts the median of 1,000 pseudosession scores. Counts of significant regions and smaller p-values do not measure prediction improvement.

aggregation.description: Paper takes median R-squared over ten repeats, then mean session corrected R-squared per region. Pinned stage3 instead takes median score minus median null medians and requires two sessions; reconcile the actual publication pipeline.

full_panel.description: The unchanged registered pre-stimulus prior-decoding finding requires all 242 Ephys and 32 WFI regional raw/corrected-R2 and null-inference profiles: 414 Ephys sessions/2289 region-sessions and 51 WFI sessions/1539 region-sessions. Preserve ten runs, source nested folds and 1000 decoding pseudosessions for each eligible cell; main and sensitivity-target/time-window profiles, cross-modality/size controls, decoded-prior choice/drift/contrast controls, the separate 171-session/806-region-session DLC panel, 124-session/660-region-session DLC+eye panel, and VISp/LGd eye controls. The present finding list contains recovered scalar summaries plus explicitly unresolved numerical controls; it is NOT the complete labeled regional finding vector. Exact region/session/condition identities and source-native result vectors must be recovered and expanded into individually identified scalar findings before admission. No regional vector is coerced to a scalar, and no arbitrary region identifiers are fabricated.

Recovered scalar summaries here do not constitute complete-panel reproduction.

Publication-linked raw numerical regional results and original seed/fold identities remain unrecovered. The illustrative 160-neuron ORBvl session must be identified; source decimals and printed region counts are exposed references, not scientific tolerances or computational proof.

Resolve the 2024 journal data release versus 2023_12_bwm_release loader, exact WFI source files and all modality/control subset rosters, including eye-only source session/region-session terminology. Cohort totals alone cannot authenticate these inputs.

Resolve journal-versus-generic author defaults for estimator/inner and outer folds, 1000 versus 200 decoding nulls, median versus mean over ten runs, session inclusion and regional aggregation; the independent choice-drift control uses 200 pseudoaction sessions and must not be mistaken for the decoding null.

No complete submitted-analysis interface or independent derivation-verification program exists. The runnable journal-metrics-v2 CLI accepts supplied per-trial predictions, targets and folds and recomputes arithmetic; it neither reconstructs authentic features/priors/nulls nor proves fitting or source-data use. A program printing the paper numbers, or supplying fabricated granular arrays, cannot qualify.

Require independently executed submitted analysis and verification of source-native per-trial feature/target/mask lineage, each run and inner/outer fold, every pseudosession target and prediction, raw and corrected score formation, source Fisher/BH maps, and exact complete-cohort coverage. Neither a prediction-file hash nor a matching aggregate establishes this derivation.

Movement and eye companions need source session-level features/predictions and matched trial identities, then separately reconstructed residual targets, residual neural fits, complete paired score vectors and source correlations. journal-metrics-v2 implements only descriptive matched movement differences; it does not implement residual/eye, size, choice/drift, contrast or feature-removal analyses.

Recover empirical mean session choice slopes and all 200 mean pseudo-slopes separately from null-corrected regional slopes, complete contrast-dependence profiles, and source feature-removal effects. Reconstruct the 17.8% Ephys/90.1% WFI regional choice significance summaries without inferring counts, session strategy-evidence/slope correlations and the WFI strategy-adjusted regional slope association. Recover the size-prediction fit inputs/coefficients for the known WFI R2 subtraction recipe and complete control result vectors. Qualitative direction or nonrejection cannot replace magnitudes, uncertainty or required companion outputs.

Scientific equivalence tolerances and uncertainty rules remain unestablished for every finding; do not infer them from rounded printing, significance thresholds or historical grader acceptance. Respect mouse dependence and repeated regions/sessions in each modality/control population.

No immutable common input, cohort/split/full-panel/observation/metric/aggregation, independent evaluator, exposure or cumulative episode budget manifests support either matched paper+data versus paper+data+author-code protocol. Both pairings remain unresolved and all four scientific outcomes unknown.
